claims.text: The initial TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase BCC material.
TiVNbTa has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 800 MPa.
TiVNbTa has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
TiVNbTa has a compressive strength of approximately 423 MPa at 1273 K.
A powder-metallurgy route based on high-energy ball milling and spark plasma sintering can produce a refractory HEA composite containing about 30 vol% TiC.
The proposed TiVNbTa composite will contain an approximately uniform dispersion of fine TiC particles in its BCC matrix.
Dispersed TiC particles will refine the TiVNbTa matrix grains.
TiC particles will create barriers to dislocation motion in TiVNbTa.
Second-phase strengthening by TiC will improve the high-temperature strength of TiVNbTa.
TiC particles will pin grain boundaries and stabilize the TiVNbTa microstructure at high temperature.
In-situ TiC formation will promote good interfacial bonding.
Good bonding associated with in-situ TiC formation will avoid significant thermal-conductivity penalties.
The TiC-reinforced TiVNbTa will have 30–50% higher yield strength at 1273 K than monolithic TiVNbTa.
The TiC-reinforced TiVNbTa will have 30–50% higher compressive strength at 1273 K than monolithic TiVNbTa.
The TiC-reinforced TiVNbTa will retain sufficient ductility for the proposed application.
The TiC-reinforced TiVNbTa will retain sufficient thermal conductivity for effective heat transfer between W and CuCrZr.
The predicted improvement is bounded to testing near 1273 K.
The cited NbMoCrTiAl composite containing TiC and Al2O3 had approximately 50% greater room-temperature compressive fracture strength than its as-cast HEA baseline.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis describes TiC as being formed in situ, whereas the intervention says TiC particles are incorporated into the matrix; these imply different reinforcement-formation routes unless precursor reactions are specified.

The intervention calls approximately 30 vol% TiC a minor fraction, although it is a substantial second-phase fraction and could conflict with the stated goals of retaining ductility and thermal conductivity.
